blockers.title: The required Linux setns-helper proof has no place in the closed retained record
evidence: The repaired Linux protocol requires a distinct dedicated helper, and normatively says to retain the helper's {pid,starttime}, the nsfd inode, and evidence that the mountinfo bytes were read after successful setns.

runPreselectionRecord is extras-rejected and admits observerProcessIdentity, mountNamespaceIdentity, and linuxSelectedMountRecordIdentity, but no helperProcessIdentity, setns result, post-setns helper namespace identity, or mountinfo-read ordering/proof field.

observerProcessIdentityShape remains the original verifier's {pid,starttime} acquisition shape. mountNamespaceIdentityShape contains only the held namespace inode plus the selected mount-record identity. Neither shape defines a nested location for the separate helper identity or successful-setns evidence, and retainedEventSchema is for later events rather than this preselection proof.

The setns source is now implementable, but a producer that adds the mandated helper evidence violates extrasRejected while a producer that omits it violates the Linux retention MUST. The helper exits, so the missing association cannot be reconstructed from the retained run record.
blockers.impact: Neither mandatory Linux slice-1 profile can produce a record that simultaneously satisfies the acquisition protocol and the closed evidence schema. Qualification must either fail or discard the very proof intended to show that mountinfo came from the held namespace.
blockers.requiredRepair: Add a closed Linux-only setnsObservation to runPreselectionRecord and its identity shapes. It should retain the helper process identity, received nsfd inode, successful setns result, the helper's post-setns /proc/self/ns/mnt inode equal to that nsfd, mountinfo read ordering or digest evidence, and helper exit status; reject extras and fail on every mismatch. Alternatively redefine the existing identities explicitly to carry both verifier and helper roles without losing either.

shouldFix.title: The closed observed-attestation union cannot be compared to the still-open signed PLATFORM-ATTESTED branch
evidence: The signed PLATFORM-ATTESTED rule still permits codesign, package db, or an unbounded 'equivalent' and defines no signed scheme/payload object. The new observedAttestation permits exactly codesign or package-db and defines payload objects only on the observed side.

evidenceJoin requires the observed scheme and payload to equal the signed identityEvidence branch, but that branch has no comparable scheme, cdhash, package name/version/digest, or per-scheme serialization paths. A lawful signed 'equivalent' has no observed union member at all.

PLATFORM-ATTESTED still describes verification of an actual resolved object, while OS ABI is required to use PATHLESS and retainedEventSchema makes resolvedObjectIdentity absent on PATHLESS events. The subject does not define which object or platform result the codesign/package-db payload attests for that mandatory pathless class.

The codesign payload retains only cdhash and the package-db payload only name/version/digest; neither closed form retains the validation result or trust assertion that makes the identifier a trusted platform attestation rather than a copied label.
shouldFix.impact: Independent verifiers cannot perform the mandated signed-to-observed equality for OS ABI, and signed profiles using the expressly permitted equivalent scheme are unrepresentable. The mandatory pathless authenticity decision remains implementation-defined.
shouldFix.requiredRepair: Roster and replace PLATFORM-ATTESTED with the same closed per-scheme signed payload union used by observedAttestation, or explicitly map each signed form to one observed form. Remove the equivalent escape or define its closed member, retain the platform-verification/trust result, and define the exact pathless OS-ABI subject each scheme attests.

shouldFix.title: The external-origin repair still lacks an exact actual-path-to-signed-origin comparison
evidence: observedOrigin.actualOrigin is called a canonicalized sensor string, but no canonicalization algorithm, symlink rule, path-versus-directory meaning, or failure rule is defined for external origins. The detailed canonicalization elsewhere applies to the verified install-root target, not this branch.

identitySerializations says actualOrigin must 'identify the same object' as resolvedObjectIdentity, but canonicalOrigin is described as an install/search origin and resolvedObjectIdentity is an authenticity identity. No field-level function relates those different domains.

The unchanged signed join says the observedOrigin object equals the signed canonicalOrigin string, while the new observed object contains actualOrigin and lookupStepIndex and evidenceJoin never explicitly requires actualOrigin bytes to equal signed canonicalOrigin bytes.
lookupStepIndex now maps to event.route, but that route binding alone does not establish that the actually resolved object's canonical path came from the signed origin.
shouldFix.impact: A trusted sensor can emit a route and object identity while producers disagree about how to derive the origin or whether it equals the signed declaration. Ambient and declared external resolutions can therefore receive different allow/refuse outcomes under conforming interpretations.
shouldFix.requiredRepair: Define whether canonicalOrigin is a full object path or search-root identity, give actualOrigin an exact symlink-resolving canonicalization and failure rule, bind it mechanically to the actual resolved path represented by resolvedObjectIdentity, and require actualOrigin bytes to equal the signed canonicalOrigin bytes at an exact named path.

advisories.title: The macOS decimal form still permits multiple byte spellings of one f_fsid value
advisories.evidence: val0 and val1 allow an optional minus followed by 1-10 decimal digits, which permits leading zeros and negative zero, while equality is numeric. Calling an int32 value little-endian is also orthogonal to its decimal text representation.
advisories.whyOnlyAdvisory: The int32 type, fixed component order, and numeric equality make the intended identity reproducible after parsing; only the claimed canonical retained bytes remain non-unique.
advisories.suggestedRepair: Require canonical signed decimal: ASCII '0' for zero, otherwise an optional minus followed by a nonzero digit and remaining digits, no leading zeros, and the exact int32 range. Drop the endianness label from decimal serialization.

advisories.title: The retired volume schema's prohibition is still version-limited to v15 producers
advisories.evidence: The retained tombstone says 'v15 producers MUST NOT emit this schema' even though the reviewed artifact is v16 and the schema is intended to remain retired for successors.
advisories.whyOnlyAdvisory: The same sentence begins RETIRED, runPreselectionRecord supersedes laterEventVolumeFields, and the active union is exhaustive, so the standing intent is clear despite the stale qualifier.
advisories.suggestedRepair: Say that no v15-or-later producer, or simply no producer, may emit the retired schema.
